reason: this is an exact object type, and TypeScript's object types are inexact: every property is still declared and still checked, but a consumer passing an object with an extra property will not be stopped
this property is write-only in Flow, and TypeScript has `readonly` and nothing on the other side, so it is published as an ordinary property a consumer may also read
TypeScript indexes only by `string`, `number` or `symbol`, so this indexer is left out and the properties it described are not declared

a spread copies one object type's properties into another and lets later ones win; a TypeScript intersection keeps both types of a shared property, which is a different type, so the spread is left out
